samples.summary: `rangeOf` uses argument spread (`Math.min(...rows)`) — replacing the removed loop-based `gridRange` reintroduces a stack-overflow crash on large pastes
samples.evidence: The delta deletes `gridRange` (which computed min/max with an explicit `for` loop over `grid.keys()`, safe for any size) and routes both `paste` (sheet.ts:2255) and `selectPastedRange` (sheet.ts:2389) through `rangeOf`, which does `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` on arrays with one element per pasted cell. V8 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` once the spread exceeds roughly 100k arguments. A plain TSV paste of a large external CSV (e.g. 20k rows x 10 cols = 200k cells) reaches `rangeOf` with a 200k-element array and throws. The throw happens before `store.beginBatch()`, so it propagates out of `Sheet.paste` into the view's catch and the paste silently fails; in `selectPastedRange` it would throw after the write, leaving the batch already ended but the exception escaping to the view handler. The previous loop had no such limit, so this is a regression introduced by this delta.

samples.summary: Reading merges live at paste time (instead of the copy-time snapshot) can create a merge that was never copied and then silently delete pasted content under it
samples.evidence: `const copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange);` is now evaluated at paste time against the *current* layout, but `this.copyBuffer.grid` is still the snapshot taken at copy time. The two can disagree in the opposite direction from the one the comment addresses: copy A1:B1 while it is NOT merged (grid holds both A1=10 and B1=20), then merge A1:B1, then paste at A5. `copiedMerges` now contains A1:B1, it passes the `isRangeInRange` check, so `pastedMerges` creates a merge A5:B5, and `clearCellsUnderMerge(A5,{rs:1,cs:2})` (sheet.ts:2339) deletes the B5 value that `setGrid` just wrote from the clipboard — content loss with no refusal and a `true` return. The same staleness applies after `shiftCells`/`moveRows`: `sourceRange` is not remapped, so a merge that has since moved *into* those coordinates is treated as copied and re-created at the destination (and, on a cut, deleted at line 2333). A snapshot validated against the live layout (drop blocks that no longer exist) would fix the reported bug without opening this one.

samples.summary: Narrowing the single-cell exemption to `destRange[0] === target` refuses a legitimate HTML paste whose single cell lands exactly on a merge anchor
samples.evidence: `writesThroughAnchor = isSameRef(destRange[0], destRange[1]) && isSameRef(destRange[0], target)`. Because `html2grid` skips empty cells but keeps the column index (grids.ts:179), a one-cell HTML grid can land offset from `target` on the *anchor* of a merged block — e.g. merge B1:C1 (anchor B1), target A1, html `x`, grid = {B1:'x'}. `destRange` is [B1,B1], `writesThroughAnchor` is false, `getMergesIntersecting([B1,B1])` returns B1:C1 which is not contained in [B1,B1], so the whole paste is refused (return false at 2287) even though writing B1 is exactly the anchor write the exemption exists to allow. The check should also allow the case where `destRange[0]` is itself a merge anchor, not only where it equals `target`.

samples.summary: `return false` on a pivot sheet makes the view keep the copy buffer forever, so the marching ants never clear
samples.evidence: `if (this.pivotDefinition) return false;` is now interpreted by both callers (spreadsheet.ts:717, worksheet.ts:4901) as "refused, keep the buffer so the user can retry". On a pivot sheet the paste can never succeed, so the buffer (and the marching-ants overlay driven by `getCopyRange`/`isCutMode`) is never cleared by any number of Ctrl+V presses. The same applies to the `else { return false; }` empty-clipboard branch at line 2247, which conflates "nothing to paste" with "refused by a merge" — the doc comment acknowledges the conflation but the callers cannot distinguish them.

samples.summary: An internal paste of an empty copied range returns `true` ("applied") although nothing was written
samples.evidence: `if (!pasteRange && grid.size === 0) return false;` only short-circuits the non-internal path. On the internal path `pasteRange` is always set, so copying an empty range (grid empty, text `''`) and pasting yields `grid.size === 0`, no `setGrid` effect, `selectPastedRange` returns early — yet `paste` returns `true`, telling the caller the paste was applied and clearing the copy buffer. Harmless today but the return contract stated in the doc comment ("`false` means nothing was written") is violated.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. coordinates.ts:18-27 `rangeOf` computes bounds with argument spread (`Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)`) over arrays holding one element per grid key, with no length cap or loop fallback (I read the entire file; no `gridRange` helper exists). Both call sites are real and reachable: sheet.ts:2255 (`pasteRange ?? rangeOf(grid)`) runs on the external TSV/HTML paste paths before `store.beginBatch()` at :2293, and sheet.ts:2389 in `selectPastedRange`, invoked at :2380 after the batch's `finally` closes. Grid size is unbounded upstream — `string2grid` (grids.ts:113-126) and `html2grid` (grids.ts:164+) create one Map entry per pasted cell with no cap, and the view handler at view/worksheet.ts:4872-4908 passes raw clipboard text straight through. V8 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` for spreads beyond roughly 100k arguments, so a routine large CSV paste (e.g. 20k x 10 = 200k cells) throws. The view's `catch` at view/worksheet.ts:4905-4907 only `console.error`s, so the paste silently fails; on the copy-buffer path (`pasteRange` precomputed at :2225 so :2255 is skipped) the throw lands at :2389 after writes committed, escaping with state already mutated. No guard makes this unreachable, so neither `already-guarded` nor `not-present` applies, and a crash plus swallowed failure on a real user path is squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists exactly as described: `copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` (sheet.ts:2204) reads the live merge map while content comes from the copy-time snapshot `copyBuffer.grid` (sheet.ts:2133-2140, 2195-2199). A merge created after the copy (mergeSelection, sheet.ts:4439-4472, which never clears copyBuffer) is fully contained in `sourceRange`, so it passes the refusal at sheet.ts:2216, becomes `pastedMerges` (2221-2224), and after `setGrid` writes the snapshot values (2295) `clearCellsUnderMerge` (2339, implementation 918-956) deletes the covered destination cells that were just written from the clipboard — silent content loss with a `true` return. The buffer survives such mutations: it is only cleared at sheet.ts:2291 (cut) and via clearCopyBuffer() from the view (view/worksheet.ts:4902, 5074; view/spreadsheet.ts:718 — Escape / successful paste), none of which fire on merge or shift. The cut path compounds it: `cutMerges` (2262-2266) is likewise computed from the live layout at an un-remapped `cutSourceRange` and those blocks are deleted at 2333-2334. No guard makes this unreachable, and data loss on a normal copy→merge→paste sequence is in-lane and blocking for the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: Single-cell paste exemption assumes the written cell is the merge anchor; an HTML paste whose grid bounding box is offset from the target writes into a covered cell of a preserved merge
finding.evidence: `const overwrittenMerges = isSameRef(destRange[0], destRange[1]) ? [] : ...` (line 2285) skips the merge check entirely for a 1x1 paste range, justified by the comment "it writes through the anchor above". That justification holds only when the single grid cell *is* `target`. For the HTML branch, `html2grid` skips empty, unstyled ``s (`packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/grids.ts:179 if (!text && !el.style.cssText) continue;`) while still advancing the column index, so pasting `x` at A1 yields a grid of only `{B1: x}`. `pasteRange = this.gridRange(grid)` is then `B1:B1`, `isSameRef` is true, the merge check is skipped, and `setGrid` (which writes raw srefs, sheet.ts:1002-1004 → store.setGrid, no anchor normalization) stores 'x' into B1 — a cell covered by the surviving A1:B1 merge. That breaks the covered-cells-hold-no-content invariant the rest of this change relies on: the value is invisible, `getCell(B1)` returns the anchor's value while the store holds another, and the content reappears on unmerge. The exemption should compare the single cell to `target` (or normalize the grid through anchors) rather than only checking that the range is collapsed.

verdict.reason: The quoted defective condition does not exist in the repository. sheet.ts:2279-2281 reads `const writesThroughAnchor = isSameRef(destRange[0], destRange[1]) && isSameRef(destRange[0], target);` — the single-cell merge-check exemption is already conjoined with an equality test against `target`, which is the anchor-normalized active cell (sheet.ts:2178, `this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell)`). That is exactly the fix the finding recommends. The finding's premise about html2grid is factually correct (grids.ts:179 skips empty unstyled cells while advancing the column index), but in that offset-grid scenario `isSameRef(destRange[0], target)` is false, so `writesThroughAnchor` is false, `getMergesIntersecting(destRange)` runs, and the partial-overwrite check at sheet.ts:2286 refuses the paste — the described write into a covered cell cannot occur. The comment at sheet.ts:2274-2277 documents this exact case as the reason the exemption is anchored on `target` rather than on the range being 1x1. Grep for `getMergesIntersecting(` confirms sheet.ts:2283 is the only paste-path use (sheet.ts:2450 is moveRangeTo, a separate flow with no 1x1 exemption), so there is no unfixed duplicate of the condition. The finding appears to describe an earlier revision of the guard.
